 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Deion Sanders is making more news, and this time, it is not for his team's on-field performance.
 In the early hours of Thursday, The Athletic published an explosive feature detailing a history of death threats made toward the Colorado head coach . While the incidents dated back to 2023, he had not publicly commented on the matter until September this year, just days before the Buffaloes began their fourth season under him.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In response to this report, the university issued this statement:
 "The safety of Coach Prime is our top priority, and we take every threat seriously. CU Athletics works closely with the CU Boulder Division of Public Safety to coordinate security efforts with Coach Prime's entire team, including his security detail, and respond appropriately to reported threats." 
 However, when Jason Whitlock got wind of the news, he instead accused Sanders of using race to deflect attention from concerns about his head coaching tenure:
 "Deion Sanders is fighting tooth and nail not to get fired. This is one of the oldest tricks in the book. Ronny Thompson planted racist letters in his office at Ball State. Deion wants you to believe no one threatens Lane Kiffin, other coaches. Deion playing the race card. Predictable." 
 Deion Sanders' history of death threats – a summary
 The first incident occurred on May 31, 2023, when two campus police officers met with Deion Sanders to discuss threatening voicemails sent to the athletic department's ticketing office phone line. At the time, he told security staffer Evis McGee:
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I guess this confirms what you are working on." 
 Those calls were eventually traced in 2023 to a relative who was believed to be outside Colorado at the time, and the case was closed. Eventually, however, the issue resurfaced. This time, it was a cluster of letters that were eventually traced back to someone in Indiana.
 Then, in January this year, Sanders' son Deion Jr. posted a video showing Michael Rhodes, the coach's head of security, telling players:
 "Don't let somebody coerce you into scanning them up on the floor, because everybody's trying to get to Coach Prime." 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement As of this writing, Sanders has not commented on The Athletic's report.
